references.text: God promised Moses that the Israelites would receive silver and gold items from the Egyptians when they left Egypt, which is fulfilled here in 11:2.
The Israelites did as Moses said and asked the Egyptians for silver and gold items, and the Lord gave the people favor with the Egyptians.
God prophesied to Abraham that his descendants would come out of slavery with great wealth, which is fulfilled through this command.
The psalm reminds us that God led the Israelites out with silver and gold, a poetic retelling of this event.
The silver and gold that the Israelites received from the Egyptians were later used to build the tabernacle and its furnishings.
Describes the same event (the plundering of the Egyptians) with complementary details about who was to ask for the items and their purpose.
Strong theological contrast: Gold is taken from the Egyptians for liberation (Ex 11), while gold is taken from the Israelites for idol worship (Ex 32).
